parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Good morning. In this module we've been looking at the production of some of the world's most important raw materials, and today it's the turn of rubber. Traditionally, natural rubber was produced on small holdings, and in case you're not familiar with the process, I'll just describe it briefly.

The first stage in the process, known as tapping, involves making an incision in the rubber tree and removing a thin layer of bark. This procedure has to be done very carefully with a special knife, because if the incision is too deep, the tree will be damaged. And a white liquid, known as latex, starts to ooze out. Next, the taper attaches a cup to the tree, made out of something simple like a coconut shell, to collect it. Tapping is usually started in the early morning, because the coolness encourages the latex to flow easily.

Later in the day, the taper goes back to each tree to get the latex, and take it to what you might call the factory, although the procedures that take place in it are relatively simple. Here it is poured into a mold, and then formic acid is added to it, and the mixture is left for a few hours.

The purpose of the formic acid is to thicken the liquid latex. So, after some time, the latex is transformed into a solid block of rubber. This block of rubber is then pressed manually, to turn it into a thin sheet.

And then, when it's thin enough, the rubber sheet is fed through a mangle. And I should point out that apart from this, no other machinery is used in the process. It's fairly simple, just a frame with two rollers, and a handle to turn them. The procedure is repeated several times to get rid of as much water as possible.

And finally, these sheets are taken to a special smoke room where they are dried. And you're then left with, what are by now, sheets of brown rubber.

These are then sold to traders, who collect them from villages and sell them on in turn.

Well, that’s the process then. Now, just a little bit about the history of rubber. Rubber was in use in America long before it became commercially important.

The rubber tree was a native of Brazil, and there’s an account from as long ago as 1525 of people in Mexico playing with rubber balls.

But it wasn’t until the 19th century that Europeans recognized the usefulness of the substance, chiefly for clothing. Various attempts were made to improve the properties of rubber. One of the key discoveries was of a process known as vulcanization, which involved heating the rubber and adding sulfur to it And the result was a substance that had a lot more strength and was also more elastic, making it suitable for a variety of uses. But the thing that gave demand for rubber a real boost was the expanding automobile industry, at the end of the 19th century, and the invention of car tires.

During the 20th century, rubber became so important that there were various attempts to develop a synthetic version But none of them resulted in a product that was able to compete with natural rubber until Germany developed a successful substitute when its supplies of the natural substance were cut off during the First World War. Later, this was accelerated when the American government built its own rubber factories. So, in economic terms, rubber’s had an outstanding position in the global market for more than 100 years.

analyses.content: 录音中说收集乳胶的杯子是由简单的东西制成的，比如椰子壳（coconut shell），题目中已有 shell，所以填 coconut。
Next, the taper attaches a cup to the tree, made out of something simple like a coconut shell, to collect it.
听到 "made out of" 就要竖起耳朵听材料，不要把 shell 重复填进去，也不要因为前面的 simple 而忽略了具体的材料名称。
Here it is poured into a mold, and then formic acid is added to it...
注意介词搭配 "poured into"，紧跟其后的就是容器名词；拼写时美式 mold 或英式 mould 都可以。
乳胶被带到工厂后，首先被倒入一个模具（poured into a mold）里。
This block of rubber is then pressed manually, to turn it into a thin sheet.
题目是 "Rubber is ... by hand"，必须填被动形式 pressed，只填 press 是语法错误的；manually 对应题目中的 by hand。
录音说橡胶块被人工按压（pressed manually）变成薄片，空缺处需要填一个被动语态的动词分词。
And I should point out that apart from this, no other machinery is used in the process.
这题很容易填成 "mangle"（轧布机/碾压机），但题目问的是“the only ... in the process”，这指的是 mangle 所属的类别——机械（machinery）。
讲师特意指出，除了前面提到的机器（mangle），流程中没有使用其他机械装置（no other machinery）。
橡胶片被带到特殊的烟熏室，在那里被干燥（where they are dried）。
And finally, these sheets are taken to a special smoke room where they are dried.
不要看到 "smoke room" 就想填 "smoked"，题目结构是 "taken to be ..."，录音中对应的动作是 dried。
These are then sold to traders, who collect them from villages and sell them on in turn.
不要填 "villagers"，录音说是从村民那里收集，卖给商人，买家是 traders。
这些橡胶片最终卖给了商人（sold to traders），题目说是 "purchased by ..."（被...购买），是被动语态转换。

groups.contentHtml:
Earliest use
• 1525: rubber were used in Mexico
19th century
• Key discovery: "vulcanisation" made rubber stronger and
• Increase in demand when rubber were invented
20th century
• Substitute for natural rubber was first developed in during First World War.

analyses.content: ...there’s an account from as long ago as 1525 of people in Mexico playing with rubber balls.
注意名词复数，录音中很清晰有 's' 的尾音；如果不填复数可能会因为语法不当扣分。
早在1525年，墨西哥人就在玩橡胶球（playing with rubber balls）。
And the result was a substance that had a lot more strength and was also more elastic...
题目是 "stronger and ..."，这暗示你需要填一个形容词（或比较级），不要只填 elastic，因为录音强调了程度 "more"，且字数限制允许两个词。
硫化过程（vulcanization）让橡胶强度更高，同时也更有弹性（also more elastic）。
录音明确交代了让橡胶需求量大增（对应Increase in demand）的原因，一个是汽车工业的扩张，另一个就是“car tires”（汽车轮胎）的发明。
你可能会一激动错填成“automobile industry”，但题目问的是什么东西被“invented”（发明），轮胎才是被发明的具体物品。
But the thing that gave demand for rubber a real boost was the expanding automobile industry at the end of the nineteenth century and the invention of car tires.
But none of them resulted in a product that was able to compete with natural rubber until Germany developed a successful substitute...
这是典型的“时间/地点干扰”，后面紧接着提到了 "American government"，但那是后来的事（Later...），题目问的是 "first developed in"，所以是德国。
在一战期间，因为天然橡胶供应中断，德国（Germany）首先开发出了成功的替代品。

groups.description: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
